post.description:
You have CVE ids and need to know whether they are known exploited, whether ransomware uses them, and what CISA requires and by when.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.0005 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

cve_ids.description: CVE ids, e.g. CVE-2021-44228 (case-insensitive; duplicates are answered once).

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Check up to 100 CVE ids against CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, read live from CISA's feed: for each id, in_kev and the full KEV entry (vendor and product, vulnerability name, date added, federal due date and required action, known ransomware campaign use, BOD 26-04 forensic triage flag, CISA's notes with vendor advisory links, CWEs), plus the catalog version and release time. What it adds over nvd-nist-gov and osv-dev: NVD carries only an in_kev flag with date added, due date and required action, and lags CISA by hours to days; it has no ransomware use, forensic triage, notes or catalog version. OSV has no KEV data.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | object | The catalog version the answer was read from. |
| `in_kev_count` | number |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `requested` | number | Distinct ids checked. |
| `results` | object[] | One result per distinct id, in request order. |
| `source_url` | string | The CISA KEV JSON feed read for this answer. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

catalog.title: CISA Catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

entry.required_action: For all affected software assets for which updates exist, the only acceptable remediation actions are: 1) Apply updates; OR 2) remove affected assets from agency networks. Temporary mitigations using one of the measures provided at https://www.cisa.gov/uscert/ed-22-02-apache-log4j-recommended-mitigation-measures are only acceptable until updates are available.
entry.short_description: Apache Log4j2 contains a vulnerability where JNDI features do not protect against attacker-controlled JNDI-related endpoints, allowing for remote code execution.
entry.vulnerability_name: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

post.description:
You need what CISA added to KEV today, this week or this month, or to answer a 'CISA adds N known exploited vulnerabilities' alert.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.0005 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous page; it keeps that page's window.

days.description:
Window length in days, ending today on CISA's US Eastern calendar; 1 means added today. CISA adds entries most weekdays, not every day.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 90; default 7.

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 100.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
CVEs CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog in the last N days (default 7, 1 for today), read live from CISA's feed, newest first, with each full KEV entry (ransomware use, forensic triage, due date, required action, notes) and the catalog version, release time and count. What it adds over nvd-nist-gov and osv-dev: NVD's KEV fields appear only after NVD syncs, so new additions are missing or partial there for hours to days, and neither NVD nor OSV can list what CISA added on a given day.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | object | The catalog version the answer was read from. |
| `next_cursor` | string | Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `results` | object[] | Matching entries, newest date_added first, then the higher CVE number. |
| `source_url` | string | The CISA KEV JSON feed read for this answer. |
| `total_matches` | number | Entries matching the filters across all pages. |
| `window` | object |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

catalog.title: CISA Catalog of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

results.required_action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

post.description:
You want every known exploited vulnerability for a vendor or product, those used by ransomware, those added or due in a date range, or the catalog page a user pasted.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.0005 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

added_from.description: Earliest date added, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Pattern: ^\s*[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\s*$.

added_to.description: Latest date added, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Pattern: ^\s*[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\s*$.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous page of the same search.

due_from.description: Earliest federal due date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Pattern: ^\s*[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\s*$.

due_to.description: Latest federal due date, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Pattern: ^\s*[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\s*$.

forensic_triage.description:
Yes keeps only CVEs that need forensic triage under BOD 26-04.

Provider reference: allowed values ["Yes", "No"].

known_ransomware_campaign_use.description:
Known keeps only CVEs CISA confirms are used in ransomware campaigns.

Provider reference: allowed values ["Known", "Unknown"].

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 25.

product.description: Case-insensitive substring of the product: Connect Secure, Exchange Server, Log4j.

query.description: Words that must all appear (case-insensitive) in the CVE id, vendor, product, vulnerability name or description: 'Roundcube', 'remote code execution', 'CVE-2024'.

url.description: A pasted cisa.gov KEV catalog page, print page, /kev or feed URL; its search_api_fulltext and field_cve values join query. Pattern: ^https?://.

vendor.description: Case-insensitive substring of the vendor or project: Ivanti, Microsoft, Apache.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Search and browse CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, read live from CISA's feed: filter by vendor, product, free text over CVE id, name and description, CWE, known ransomware campaign use, BOD 26-04 forensic triage, date-added range and due-date range; paged, newest additions first. Accepts a pasted cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog URL including its ?search_api_fulltext= and ?field_cve= forms. What it adds over nvd-nist-gov and osv-dev: catalog-wide browsing and vendor or product grouping (all KEVs for Ivanti), ransomware and forensic triage filters and CISA's notes, none of which NVD or OSV can query.

The response contains the tool result directly.
